title: Pre-register the four masking-rate rows
headline: The plan was fixed before any run, and one failed check now decides a row
setup: A pre-registration writes the plan down before any training or battle, so a result cannot bend it afterwards. This one fixed four rows, each a way to train and sample the model, and ran six quick checks that need no battle. One of those checks now decides whether one row is battled at all.
alt: The plan fixed four rows before any run. Five checks passed. The t check read 0.005 and 0.008, under its bar of 0.01, so Per-field, corrected t is battled only if the same check reaches the bar on the new model. The battles can detect a gap of 0.001, and training luck alone has reached 0.0019.
terms: One way to train and sample the model. Four are compared. The control is Per-field, uncorrected t: our own settings
The chance a field is hidden in training. Per-field, ours: species are almost never hidden. Linear, the papers': every field has the same chance
The t at which training hid as many fields as are still hidden at this pass
Measures how far the model's choices move when told the corrected t: 0 is no change. Under 0.01, the correction cannot matter, and the row is not battled
The smallest difference in error the planned battles can tell from noise: 0.001
The gap two trainings of one recipe show by chance alone: up to 0.0019 in error. A win under 0.002 is treated as luck
The training teams whose win-rate labels come only from battles that shuffle a team's six Pokémon
